images.title: Sort number systems by two questions
images.purpose: Shows the core move of the numeral system sorter: the same number in three systems dropped into a grid that asks about place value and a zero symbol.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One two by two grid in the centre with headers on top and left, three cards placed in three cells, one cell empty.
images.exact_structure: A two by two grid with thin dark lines. Column headers on top: place value (left), no place value (right). Row headers on the left: zero symbol (top), no zero symbol (bottom). Top left cell: a teal (#0072B2) card showing 305. Bottom left cell: an amber (#E69F00) card showing a rod numeral for 305: three vertical rods, a blank gap, five vertical rods. Bottom right cell: a reddish purple (#CC79A7) card showing CCCV. Top right cell empty. Exactly 3 cards. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Only a system with both place value and a zero symbol writes every number without confusion.
images.description: Shows the core move of the numeral system sorter: the same number in three systems dropped into a grid that asks about place value and a zero symbol.
images.context: Hindu 305, Chinese rods 305 with a blank tens place, Roman CCCV.

image_decisions.why: The doer image shows the sorter's single action: placing a numeral in the grid by two properties.
